call_points.text: Beauty & Cosmetics grew over 20% and now accounts for 54% of the portfolio.
EAP led regional growth at 34.3%, Americas 29.4%, Europe 20.2%, AMESA 17%.
Capex is running ahead of the curve, contributing to higher net debt.
Indovida merger received CCI approval; transaction on track within planned timeline.
Indovida Q1 EBITDA was about ₹383 Cr, with 25% revenue growth and 27% margin.
Europe margins below mid-teens target on transitional costs; recovery expected in coming quarters.
Beauty & Cosmetics market share at 8%, targeted to double to 16% in the next few years.
Management reiterated long-term revenue growth guidance of 11% to 13%, with EBITDA growth slightly outpacing revenue.
Nearly 50% of contracts have raw material pass-through; price adjustments will be executed proactively to offset Middle East cost inflation.
Dividends are paused until the Indovida share swap merger is completed, guided for Q4 FY27.
Steady-state effective tax rate guided in the range of 18% to 22%, driven by country mix.
Americas FY26 revenue grew 21.1% YoY, while EAP grew 15.7% YoY.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The GST department conducted an audit on the Company under Section 65 of the Central Goods and Service Tax Act, 2017 ("CGST Act"), for the period April 2019 to March 2023, pursuant to which a Show Cause Notice dated 18.08.2025 was issued alleging short‑payment of GST amounting to Rs. 5,32,960/- under the Reverse Charge Mechanism on services received from working director of the Company for FY 2021‑22. The Company submitted written replies and supporting documents contesting the proposed demand. The matter remained pending in adjudication until issuance of the order dated 23.12.2025 by the GST department.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Neeta P. Karbhari, Superintendent, CGST – Thane Rural, Division‑VI, Range‑II, Office of the Assistant Commissioner, Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance
tax_litigation.status: The Company, on 24.12.2025, received the Adjudication order dated 23.12.2025 under Section 73(1) read with section 73(9) of the CGST Act, read with relevant provisions of the Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, confirming a demand of Rs. 5,32,960/- along with interest under Section 50 and a penalty of Rs. 53,296/- for short payment of GST under Reverse Charge Mechanism on services received from working director of the Company for FY 2021‑22. The Company maintains its stand that this is not taxable under the current GST framework (Schedule III of the CGST Act) and department circular no 140/10/2020 – GST Dated 10th June, 2020. The Company shall file a formal appeal before the Appellate Authority within the prescribed timelines.

operating_notes.text: Incurred ₹6.7 Cr exceptional cost during FY26 due to closure of a factory unit in a subsidiary.
Board approved merger of Indovida India Private Limited with EPL Limited on March 29, 2026, incurring ₹15.6 Cr in advisory costs in FY26.
Recyclable tube solutions comprised 38% of total volume in FY26 compared to 33% in FY25.
ROCE reached 19.0% in FY26, up 96 bps YoY.
Thailand greenfield capex was $5 million; plant validation ongoing with volumes expected to ramp in FY27.
Sustainable tube formats contributed 38% of total sales in Q4 FY26.
CCI approved the Scheme of Amalgamation of Indovida India Private Limited into EPL Limited under Section 31(1) of the Competition Act, 2002.
Beauty & Cosmetics accounts for 54% of the portfolio and grew over 20% in Q1FY27.
Sustainable tubes account for 44% of the overall product mix.
Beauty & Cosmetics market share is 8%, with management targeting 16% over the next few years.
Epsilon Bidco Pte. Ltd., holding 0 shares (0%), was approved by the board for re-classification from promoter to public category.

timeline.summary: Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹1,300.5 Cr (+17.6% YoY), net profit ₹103.3 Cr (-10.7% YoY).
EPL Limited presented its Q4FY26 investor presentation, highlighting 20.2% EBITDA margin and expansion of Beauty & Cosmetics mix to 53%.
EPL Limited hosted an analysts/investor conference call on May 14, 2026, to discuss Q4FY26 and FY26 audited financial results, with audio recording available at the company’s website.
EPL held its Q4FY26 earnings call, maintaining 11-13% long-term revenue growth guidance and projecting merger completion by Q4FY27.
CCI approved the Scheme of Amalgamation of Indovida India Private Limited into EPL Limited.
EPL raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to high teens from early double digits on its Q1FY27 call, after 25.3% reported and 20% underlying revenue growth.
EPL reported insider trading code violations by a designated person who was issued a caution.
EPL received no-adverse-observation letters from BSE and NSE on October 19, 2026, for the proposed amalgamation of Indovida India Private Limited.
EPL submitted an application to BSE and NSE on October 23, 2026, for the reclassification of Epsilon Bidco Pte. Ltd. from promoter to public category.
EPL Limited issued and allotted Commercial Papers amounting to ₹60 Crore on October 27, 2026.

status_history.evidence: CCI conveyed approval to the Scheme of Amalgamation of Indovida India Private Limited with EPL Limited vide letter dated May 26, 2026.

watchlist.text: Input cost inflation and margin compression risk from Middle East crisis

watchlist.response: CFO said the increase was largely inventory, driven by higher raw material prices and safety stock, and that receivable days and aging remain under control.
watchlist.text: Working capital rose about ₹180 Cr in Q1FY27, more than the ₹170 Cr full-year FY26 increase, raising questions on receivables.

watchlist.response: Management said the operational challenges have been identified and are getting disproportionate focus, with margins expected to progressively recover.
watchlist.text: Europe margins are below the mid-teens target due to transitional costs.

watchlist.response: CFO attributed the gap to a higher effective tax rate versus a low base last year, guiding FY27 ETR at 20-22%.
